Class ScalaIterableSerde<T>

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.scala.serde.ScalaIterableSerde<T>
Type Parameters:
T - The element type
All Implemented Interfaces:
io.micronaut.serde.Serializer<scala.collection.Iterable<T>>, io.micronaut.serde.util.CustomizableSerializer<scala.collection.Iterable<T>>
@Singleton @Requires(classes=io.micronaut.serde.Serializer.class) public final class ScalaIterableSerde<T> extends Object implements io.micronaut.serde.util.CustomizableSerializer<scala.collection.Iterable<T>>
Serialization for the Scala collections, which are a JSON array like any other.

They are not java.util.Collections, so Micronaut Serialization has no serializer for them and falls back to introspecting the concrete type -- $colon$colon, the cons cell behind a List, which no one declared and which carries nothing meaningful. A member declared List[String] therefore failed both ways round.

Writing iterates, which every Scala collection supports, so one serializer naming the most general Scala collection type covers all of them. Reading does not work that way and lives in ScalaCollectionDeserializer.
